Mixing becomes negligible, so the expected normal order is observed: $\sigma 2p_z$ fills before $\pi 2p_x, \pi 2p_y$. Statement (ii) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (iii): Neutral $\text{N}_2$ has 14 electrons with the highest occupied MO being $\sigma 2p_z^2$. Ionization to form $\text{N}_2^+$ removes one electron from $\sigma 2p_z$, leaving one unpaired electron. The bond order becomes $\frac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5$, making $\text{N}_2^+$ paramagnetic. Statement (iii) is correct.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (iv): $\text{Ne}_2$ has 20 electrons, completely filling all bonding and antibonding molecular orbitals up to $\sigma^* 2p_z^2$ ($N_b = 10, N_a = 10$). $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 10}{2} = 0$. With zero bond order, $\text{Ne}_2$ does not exist as a bound molecule. Statement (iv) is incorrect. Hence, only statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the polyatomic oxoanions in List I with their isostructural counterparts having the identical molecular geometry in List II:
List I:
(A) $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$
(B) $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$
(C) $\text{NO}_2^-$
(D) $\text{ClO}_3^-$
List II:
(I) $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ (tetrahedral)
(II) $\text{NO}_3^-$ (trigonal planar)
(III) $\text{SO}_3^{2-}$ (trigonal pyramidal)
(IV) $\text{O}_3$ (bent / angular)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the geometry of each species using steric number ($\sigma$ bonds + lone pairs).
Step 2: For $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$, steric number = 3 ($3\sigma$ bonds, 0 lone pairs) $\rightarrow$ trigonal planar. Similarly, $\text{NO}_3^-$ has steric number = 3 ($3\sigma$ bonds, 0 lone pairs) $\rightarrow$ trigonal planar. Both are isostructural (A)-(II).
Step 3: For $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, steric number = 4 ($4\sigma$ bonds, 0 lone pairs) $\rightarrow$ tetrahedral. $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ also has steric number = 4 ($4\sigma$ bonds, 0 lone pairs) $\rightarrow$ tetrahedral. Both are isostructural (B)-(I).
Step 4: For $\text{NO}_2^-$, steric number = 3 ($2\sigma$ bonds, 1 lone pair) $\rightarrow$ bent/angular. Ozone ($\text{O}_3$) also has steric number = 3 ($2\sigma$ bonds, 1 lone pair on central oxygen) $\rightarrow$ bent/angular. Both are isostructural (C)-(IV).
Step 5: For $\text{ClO}_3^-$, chlorine has 7 valence electrons, forms 3 bonds and has 1 lone pair (steric number = 4) $\rightarrow$ trigonal pyramidal. Sulfite ion ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$) also has steric number = 4 ($3\sigma$ bonds, 1 lone pair on sulfur) $\rightarrow$ trigonal pyramidal. Both are isostructural (D)-(III). Thus, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding resonance stabilization and average bond orders in common oxoanions:
(i) In the phosphate ion ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$), all four phosphorus-oxygen bonds are of identical length with an average $\text{P}-\text{O}$ bond order of $1.25$.
(ii) In the perchlorate ion ($\text{ClO}_4^-$), all four chlorine-oxygen bonds are equivalent with an average $\text{Cl}-\text{O}$ bond order of $1.75$.
(iii) In the nitrate ion ($\text{NO}_3^-$), all three nitrogen-oxygen bonds are equivalent with an average $\text{N}-\text{O}$ bond order of $1.33$.
(iv) In the sulfate ion ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$), resonance stabilization causes two bonds to remain permanently single and two to remain permanently double without electron delocalization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Calculate the bond order for each oxoanion using the formula: $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{\text{Total number of bonds between central atom and oxygens}}{\text{Total number of resonating positions}}$.
Step 2: In $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$, phosphorus forms one $\text{P}=\text{O}$ double bond and three $\text{P}-\text{O}^-$ single bonds (total 5 bonds over 4 oxygen positions). $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25$. All $\text{P}-\text{O}$ bonds are identical by symmetry. Statement (i) is correct.
Step 3: In $\text{ClO}_4^-$, chlorine forms three $\text{Cl}=\text{O}$ double bonds and one $\text{Cl}-\text{O}^-$ single bond (total 7 bonds over 4 oxygen positions). $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{7}{4} = 1.75$. All $\text{Cl}-\text{O}$ bonds are equivalent. Statement (ii) is correct.
Step 4: In $\text{NO}_3^-$, nitrogen forms one double bond and two single bonds (total 4 bonds over 3 oxygen positions). $\text{Bond Order} = \frac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$. Statement (iii) is correct.
Step 5: In $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, sulfur forms two double bonds and two single bonds (total 6 bonds over 4 positions). Resonance delocalizes the $\pi$ electrons evenly over all four oxygens, making all four $\text{S}-\text{O}$ bonds completely equivalent with a bond order of $\frac{6}{4} = 1.50$. They are not localized into permanent single and double bonds. Statement (iv) is incorrect. Hence, only statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are correct.
